projects.name: EBOLOWA MASTER PLAN
projects.seoDescription: A master plan for Ebolowa, Cameroon: an education route threading circular timber pavilions through the rainforest, linking housing, culture and sport.
imageAlts: Circular timber pavilions of the Ebolowa master plan set among Cameroon's rainforest canopy

projects.description:
“Ebolowa New Dream Town” is envisioned as a new important urban pole for the capital city of Cameroon South Region, while at the same time, it serves as a benchmark development and reference model for the other countries of Central Africa.

The project is founded on the belief that education is the most powerful driver of rapid and sustainable development, particularly for nations rich in natural resources.

Pole A & B could very well represent 1 Pole or differently even an “education route” with 3 very important schools at the regional and national level. Bantu museum is also added as an educational resource for the local community and to learn more about the history of the Cameroonian people’s ethnic provenance. 4 education facilities lined up in one axis will recall to the people of Ebolowa, Cameroon and visitors the importance of education for the future of the country.

The project emphasizes through design the “education route” that extends from east to west, connecting four educational institutions: the Music Faculty “Chantal Biya,” Art School “Dritero Agolli,” Bantu Museum, and Professional School. The route toward knowledge starts in both directions, west and east, with an evident symbolic gate styled as a transparent pavilion where you find architecture and nature in one.

The modernism of regular and irregular simple geometries of volumes and architecture elements is transformed into an organic interpretation of the landscaped context, local materials, and living mentality.

Everything is very well connected on a larger scale with a proposed pedestrian cycle path that starts from the city center and crosses its future different urban poles.

The first one, “Ebolowa New Dream Town,” also accommodates to the south of the “education route,” a sports center, a conservation park for endangered species, eco-friendly and outstanding housing for tourists and visitors’ hospitality, dormitory and social housing for students and professors.

projects.description:
Alem Aga Farm is a mark of modernity in a distinguished location along the transit route from Vlora to the Albanian South Coast. It functions as a clearly defined stop where travelers can pause to dine and purchase local bio-products from the region, including meat, eggs, cheese, fruits, vegetables, olives, honey, and other artisanal goods. The most striking part of the building, from the visual perspective of the access, is a glass volume designed as a greenhouse, filled with natural light and lush greenery.

Visitors immediately get a sense of the experience they can expect, reflected in the character of the building.

The green terrace enhances this feeling. The main concept of the functional and volumetric design is a fusion of architecture, the specific arts involved, and nature.

One volume appears visually strong and stable, representing sustainability, while the other is fragile and transparent, signifying social imbalances. Together, they operate dynamically to achieve the appropriate EQUILIBRIUM.

projects.description:
Concert Hall Gërmia is a unique opportunity for Prishtina to revive a notable building from the past with a fresh contemporary vision that clearly looks to the future.

This key conceptual principle of the architectural intervention preserves the facade of the 1970s building as a historical trace for future generations, reintroducing the original geometries of its most significant elements into the new design.

The new building extensions, incorporating entirely new and important functions, also look toward the future, interpreting the integration of the original facade with transparent glass modules inspired by the geometry of the aluminum pattern, while respecting the original design.

The transition between two epochs is expressed as a fusion in the proposal. Above all, our intervention is urban, providing the most direct connection between the southwest and northeast areas of the city center, while passing through the city’s most important public space, “Skanderbeg” Square. Almost all previously atrophied spaces are activated, and the Concert Hall Gërmia building itself becomes the protagonist of the urban landscape, offering a 360° experience and the full prominence that such a building deserves.
